_note: Collaboration logic shown when a card on the Head of Operations org chart is clicked. Cards are matched by name first (for to-be-hired cards), then by role.

People Ops / Culture Manager.owns: Day-to-day people operations, onboarding, performance processes, manager support, team engagement, contractor and employee administration.
People Ops / Culture Manager.works: Performance systems, workforce planning, organisational gaps, onboarding effectiveness, capacity issues and improving how managers manage people.
People Ops / Culture Manager.line: People Ops runs the function. Head of Operations sets the direction, manages the role and remains accountable for the function performing properly.

Technology Operations Associate.owns: Building, testing and maintaining internal systems, automations, integrations, data flows and operational tools.
Technology Operations Associate.works: Capacity models, forecasting, margin controls, reporting, internal software, AI tools, open-source solutions and reducing manual work or software cost.
Technology Operations Associate.line: Head of Operations decides which business problems matter and what should be prioritised. Technology Operations executes and helps find the best technical solution.

Legal Consultant.owns: Specialist legal advice on contracts, employment and contractor matters, policies, commercial agreements and other legal risks.
Legal Consultant.works: Making sure company structures and processes are legally workable, especially across international teams and operational changes.
Legal Consultant.line: Legal advises on risk and legal requirements. Head of Operations decides how that advice is implemented operationally across the business.

Social Media Manager.owns: Day-to-day company social channels, content execution, publishing, community activity and agreed social performance targets.
Social Media Manager.works: Targets, reporting, processes, tools, productivity and making sure Social supports wider company priorities.
Social Media Manager.line: This sits under Head of Operations temporarily because there is currently no senior Marketing owner. It should move under Marketing once the right leadership layer exists.

Head of Marketing + PR.owns: Overall company marketing, brand positioning, PR, communications and marketing strategy.
Head of Marketing + PR.works: Marketing systems, reporting, resources, technology, processes and cross-functional projects that require Sales, Marketing or Operations to work together.
Head of Marketing + PR.line: Marketing owns the strategy and results. Operations helps build the infrastructure and removes operational blockers.

Chief Financial Officer.owns: Financial reporting, cash, budgeting, accounting, banking, financial planning and the Finance team.
Chief Financial Officer.works: Operational forecasting, cost visibility, resource economics, margin controls, investment modelling and making sure operational and financial data connect properly.
Chief Financial Officer.line: Finance owns the financial numbers. Operations owns the live operating systems and data that help explain and influence what happens before those numbers become final.

Head of Delivery / Delivery Director.owns: Campaign Delivery, campaign performance, quality, timelines, team performance and Delivery margin.
Head of Delivery / Delivery Director.works: Margin-control infrastructure, capacity models, resource planning, performance reporting, process improvement and identifying recurring delivery problems.
Head of Delivery / Delivery Director.line: Delivery owns the outcome. Operations builds the controls, systems and visibility that make it easier to achieve and hold people accountable for it.

Chief Sales Officer / Partnerships Leade.owns: New business, pipeline generation, sales performance, commercial relationships and Sales team targets.
Chief Sales Officer / Partnerships Leade.works: Pipeline forecasting, CRM infrastructure, reporting, lead flow, sales capacity, automation and understanding what future pipeline means for the rest of the company.
Chief Sales Officer / Partnerships Leade.line: Sales owns winning revenue. Operations makes sure the systems, data and downstream planning are ready to support it.

Paid Marketing Director.owns: Paid Media strategy, performance, team delivery and client results within Paid Media.
Paid Marketing Director.works: Systems, reporting, capacity, tooling, resource requirements and cross-functional operational improvements.
Paid Marketing Director.line: Paid Media owns specialist performance. Operations supports the structure and infrastructure around it.

Campaign Manager.owns: Day-to-day campaign execution, creators, timelines, deliverables and campaign hygiene.
Campaign Manager.works: Processes, tools, automation, workload data, capacity models and recurring delivery problems.
Campaign Manager.line: Campaign Manager owns execution. Operations improves the system they execute within.

Account Manager.owns: Day-to-day client relationship, account performance, renewals, growth opportunities and commercial coordination.
Account Manager.works: CRM structure, targets, reporting, forecasting, client processes and cross-functional issues affecting the account.
Account Manager.line: Account Manager owns the client relationship. Operations builds the infrastructure around how accounts are managed and measured.

Client Director.owns: Senior client relationships, strategic account growth, commercial performance and oversight of key accounts and Account Managers.
Client Director.works: Account targets, reporting, forecasting, processes, team structure and issues affecting several departments.
Client Director.line: Client Director owns client strategy and account performance. Operations supports the structure, data and accountability around it.

Partnerships Director.owns: Winning new clients, developing commercial relationships and turning opportunities into revenue.
Partnerships Director.works: CRM, pipeline reporting, forecasting, lead flow, automation and making sure future business can be supported operationally.
Partnerships Director.line: Partnerships owns winning the business. Operations connects pipeline with the rest of the company.

Director of New Business.owns: New business strategy, major opportunities, lead generation channels and improving how the company wins new clients.
Director of New Business.works: Sales systems, lead generation infrastructure, pipeline data, forecasting, automation and testing new routes to market.
Director of New Business.line: New Business owns generating and converting opportunities. Operations builds the infrastructure that helps it scale.

CEO.owns: Company direction, major strategic decisions, senior leadership, investors and overall business performance.
CEO.works: Turning priorities into execution, company structure, major operational decisions, performance visibility and issues that genuinely need CEO involvement.
CEO.line: Operations removes operational complexity from the CEO and brings clear recommendations rather than raw problems.

Payment Managers.owns: Day-to-day payments, payment processing, creator and supplier payments, reconciliations and related Finance administration.
Payment Managers.works: Payment workflows, automation, system improvements, handovers between teams and removing unnecessary manual work.
Payment Managers.line: Payment Managers own payment execution under Finance. Operations improves how the process works across the company.

Creative Strategists.owns: Campaign creative strategy, concepts, briefs and creative recommendations that improve campaign performance.
Creative Strategists.works: Workflow, capacity, tools, reporting and how Creative connects with Sales, Account Management and Delivery.
Creative Strategists.line: Creative owns the creative thinking. Operations makes sure the function fits efficiently into the wider operating model.

Senior Campaign Managers.owns: Performance of the campaigns under their responsibility, including margin, timelines, quality, risk and Campaign Manager performance.
Senior Campaign Managers.works: Margin controls, capacity, workload allocation, performance data, process improvements and recurring Delivery issues.
Senior Campaign Managers.line: Senior Campaign Managers own campaign outcomes. Operations provides the control, data and systems around that accountability.

Head of Delivery and Performance.owns: The whole Delivery function, including campaign performance, margin, quality, timelines, capacity and performance of the Delivery team.
Head of Delivery and Performance.works: Margin-control infrastructure, capacity modelling, forecasting, systems, resource planning and structural improvements across Delivery.
Head of Delivery and Performance.line: Head of Delivery owns Delivery results. Operations builds the wider control and infrastructure that helps Delivery achieve them consistently.

Chief Sales Officer.owns: Sales strategy, revenue targets, Sales leadership, pipeline performance and overall new business performance.
Chief Sales Officer.works: Sales reporting, CRM, forecasting, lead infrastructure, capacity planning, automation and the operational impact of future revenue.
Chief Sales Officer.line: Chief Sales Officer owns revenue generation. Operations makes sure the business has the systems, information and capacity to support that growth.
